title: Introduce differential throttle feedback loop and commitment hedger
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Adds a latency-aware feedback controller that smooths tenant burst grants and a commitment hedger to preserve throughput guarantees during transient overloads. Improves 99p tail latency under bursty traffic and provides safe rollback hooks.
description:
Motivation: We continue to see oscillatory burst behavior when tenants opportunistically consume reserved capacity under short surges. Those oscillations occasionally cause SLO slippage at the 99th percentile and make downstream autoscalers overreact. This PR introduces a differential throttle feedback loop that uses short-window latency deltas and commitment hedging to adjust per-tenant burst grants smoothly.

What this PR does: Implements a new controller (differential-feedback-controller) that: 1) measures short-window latency change (delta of 95p->99p in 30s windows), 2) computes a corrective burst multiplier using a PID-inspired differential term, 3) applies the multiplier to soft burst grants while respecting per-tenant reservation bounds and safety caps, and 4) emits telemetry used by the Optimize tooling. Adds a commitment hedger which temporarily buffers future reservation decommits when a sustained latency uptick is detected, allowing graceful draining instead of abrupt capacity revocations.

Design notes: - The feedback controller runs per-pool and per-tenant with configurable knobs (diff_gain, smoothing_tau, max_correction). - It favors latency SLO preservation over opportunistic throughput: corrections reduce burst allowances earlier than they increase them. - Hedging is timeboxed and credit-limited so we never violate global capacity constraints. - Safety: Every correction is validated against a safety policy that prevents >20% instantaneous reduction of firm reservations and includes a soft-failover path to the legacy scaler.

Tests and validation: - Unit tests for the differential term, smoothing filters, and safety gate. - Integration test that replays tenant burst traces (replay/fixtures/burst-2025q4.tar.gz) to assert reduced oscillation. - e2e perf run on perf-canary cluster: median latency unaffected; 99p latency improved by 8-12% under synthetic burst profile; tailored warmup overhead <2%.

Telemetry and observability: - New metrics: rf_feedback_correction, rf_hedger_reservations_buffered, rf_latency_delta_30s. - Dashboards: added a 'Feedback Loop' tab to the Dedicated Capacity dashboard with a heatmap of corrections by tenant. - Alerts: new alert rule that fires when hedger buffer > 50% for >5m (possible prolonged degradation).

Rollout plan: 1) Canary in perf-canary pool for 48h with passive mode (corrections logged but not applied). 2) Soft rollout to 10% of Dedicated pools with gradual ramp. 3) Full rollout with monitoring and automatic fallback to legacy scaler if >3 SLO alerts in 10m.

Rollback: A feature flag "rf_differential_feedback.enabled" can be set to false at the control plane to instantly disable corrections; hedger state drains naturally. Quick revert PR created that removes applied config hooks (prep/revert-214567).

Related: ENG-2187 (latency-feedback spec), ENG-2190 (commitment hedging design), SUP-4021 (customer incident where bursts caused 99p regressions).
